commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[zephyr] Keep stage counters separate from same-name pipeline counters (#10982)

A stage counter and a pipeline counter with the same name are now
separate counters. Before, `pipeline.update_counter("metric", 1)`
followed by `stage("stg").update_counter("metric", 2)` on one worker
produced a single entry: pipeline scope read 3 and the stage read
nothing, so `get_counters(stage="stg")` and stage stats missed the
value.

Workers stored counters in a dict keyed by name, with the stage as a
field on the entry, and every snapshot, heartbeat merge and subprocess
counter file kept that shape. Counters are now keyed by
`CounterKey(stage, name)` from the worker through the snapshots the
coordinator receives, and `CounterEntry` no longer carries a stage.
Output that leaves this path stays keyed by name: worker and stage
stats, `get_counters()`, the execution result and published telemetry.
With no stage filter, those views still fold a name's scopes into one
value, as before. One helper, `counters_by_name`, does that folding
everywhere.

Aggregation modes stay per counter name, as `set_aggregation` documents,
and are kept in their own map. `set_aggregation` no longer creates a
zero-valued placeholder entry, which was always created under pipeline
scope.

The test that #10883 marked as an expected failure now passes, and a new
test sends one worker's snapshot through the coordinator. The Zephyr
suite passes locally except nine `test_runners.py` tests that need the
embedded Finelog server extension, which is not built in this checkout;
CI runs those and the affected Levanter and Marin suites.

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[grafana] Show capacity-skipped canary runs as skipped (#10977)

The Grafana nightly matrix now shows a canary run that Iris cancelled
for lack of capacity as "⊘ Skipped", not as passed or failed. This
follows the review discussion on #10909.

Such a run finishes green, so the matrix got it wrong in two ways. Hero
GB200 and Grug multislice have no duration baseline, so a skipped day
showed as ✓ Passed. The datakit lanes expect at least 65 minutes, so a
short skipped run tripped the too-short check and showed as × Failed.

Each nightly lane now names the workflow step that runs only when the
canary skipped, or none if the lane never skips. That step is "Note a
skipped day" for the five canaries that can skip. For a successful run
on such a lane, the bridge reads the run's jobs from GitHub and marks
the run skipped if that step succeeded. GitHub lists a step whose `if`
was false with conclusion "skipped", so only a successful step counts. A
re-run keeps its run id but gets a new attempt number, and a completed
attempt never changes, so the bridge caches the answer per run attempt
and makes one extra request per attempt. The panel shows skipped cells
in slate grey, counts them in the "Today" summary and lists them in the
legend.

Hero GB200 already has this step on main, so its skips show correctly as
soon as this merges. The other four lanes get the step from #10975 and
show skips once that PR merges too. The two PRs can merge in either
order.

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[ci] Post a Slack notice when a canary skips for lack of capacity (#10975)

Scheduled canaries now post a neutral Slack message when Iris cancels
them for lack of capacity, so a skipped day is visible without being
reported as a failure. This follows the review discussion on #10909.

Five canaries cancel themselves when they cannot get capacity: hero
GB200, Grug multislice, and datakit tiers 1 to 3. Such a run ends green,
so the existing failure alert stays quiet and nothing is posted at all.
A lane could go several days without running and nobody would hear about
it.

Each of these workflows now exports the `resource_exhausted` output that
`iris_monitor.py wait` already writes, and a new `notify-skipped` job
posts ":white_circle: <canary> skipped: no capacity, so it did not run.
This is not a failure." with the run link. Like the existing alerts, it
fires only for scheduled runs. The four canaries other than hero also
gain hero's "Note a skipped day" step, which adds a notice and a
step-summary line to the run.

This is independent of #10909, which makes the hero canary's queue
timeout fire while a Kueue-held gang still reports RUNNING; with both
merged, a day with no free GB200 rack produces this message instead of a
failure alert. #10977 makes the Grafana nightly matrix show these runs
as skipped; it reads the "Note a skipped day" step this PR adds.

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[ci] Keep the queue timeout until a child task runs (#10909)

`iris_monitor.py wait --child-wait-timeout` now keeps its queue deadline
until one of the child's tasks is RUNNING. Before, it dropped the
deadline as soon as the child job reported RUNNING, but Iris reports a
job RUNNING before any task starts.

On the GB200 cluster, a Kueue-gated 16-node gang sits as a RUNNING job
with every task BUILDING. The hero canary therefore waited past its
five-hour window until the Actions step timed out at 340 minutes, so a
day without a rack became a "canary failed" Slack alert and a Loom
triage session instead of a skip. That happened on both the first manual
run and the first scheduled run.

The check is wrong beyond GB200: of 200 RUNNING jobs on the marin
controller, 67 had no running task (40 all PENDING, 27 all BUILDING).
None reported RUNNING without task counts, so canaries that do start
keep dropping the deadline as before.

Fixes #10897

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[grug] Get ring_filtered's routing-weight gradient from the down projection (#10345)

Compute ring_filtered's routing-weight gradient from tensors that the
down projection's backward pass already holds, so the expert outputs no
longer have to be kept for the backward pass. On one EP8 rank of June
Snowball this cuts peak memory by 16.5 GiB and step time by 2.9%, and
the production per-GPU batch now fits in memory.

On the expert side, ring_filtered scales each expert output row y [A, H]
by its routing weight w, then sums the rows back into tokens. A is the
number of (token, expert) assignments a rank receives and H is the
hidden size. The gradient of w is the dot product <dout, y>, where dout
is the gradient flowing into the combined output. To compute it,
`save_moe` kept y in memory for the backward pass, and `recompute_all`
ran the down projection a second time.

y is not needed. Write the down projection as y = hidden W2. Its
backward pass already computes dy = w * dout and dhidden = dy W2^T. So
<hidden, dhidden> = w <hidden W2, dout> = w <y, dout>, and the
routing-weight gradient is <hidden, dhidden> / w. A zero weight gets a
zero gradient. One custom VJP, `_down_project_combine`, now covers both
the down projection and the combine, and computes the gradient this way.

The forward pass and the gradients of x, w13 and w2 are unchanged. The
routing-weight gradient matches the old one up to bfloat16 rounding.

Measured on one MI350X running one EP8 rank of June Snowball with
`save_moe`:

| Batch per GPU | Step before (s) | Step after (s) | Peak memory before
(GiB) | Peak memory after (GiB) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | 1.427 | 1.385 (-2.9%) | 207.0 | 190.5 |
| 16 | out of memory (XLA requests 270) | — | out of memory | 235.5 |

Batch 16 per GPU is each rank's share of the production batch of 128 on
8 GPUs. The ring_filtered tests pass on CPU and on MI350X.

This applies directly to main now that #9880 has merged. It edits code
next to #10343's change in `ep_ring_filtered.py`, so whichever of the
two merges second needs a rebase that keeps both custom VJPs. Part of
#9812.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[finelog] Open indexed files as execution demands them (#10936)

Object-backed queries now build plans from captured catalog metadata and
prepare indexes and Parquet files when execution opens each file.
Filtered unordered LIMIT queries can stop preparing the remaining files
once DataFusion has enough exact matches. Global sorts and aggregates
retain their complete scan semantics.

Compose the existing DataFusion file opener and Parquet decoder with
per-file index pruning, shared footer metadata, and unified object range
reads. Index failures and projection failures before the projection's
first row fall back to the source. A required source missing when
reached fails the query.

Use the snapshotted table's maximum query lifetime as an absolute read
deadline starting at snapshot capture, so planning consumes that
lifetime. Cancel warming admitted by forwarding reads when the read
fails or is cancelled. Keep concurrency permits held until cache I/O and
index parsing workers finish, including after query cancellation.
Cache-fill writes use an independent worker pool; remote range reads
follow the per-query execution window. Read diagnostics retain phase
timings, opened/pruned files, range requests, and index decline reasons
on failure or cancellation.

[Reviewed
design](https://loom.oa.dev/s/48pzusj4/artifacts/finelog-demand-driven-execution).
[Incident record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/926).

On the same 128-file indexed corpus, five alternating fresh-process runs
gave median range-backed early LIMIT times of 84→35 ms and full
aggregate times of 70→44 ms; global sort rose from 51→81 ms. The copied
production-sample LIMIT remained about 35 ms. The corrected release
`3c759c7555` returned 100 valid inference matches on the Marin hub in
0.659 seconds, with repeats at 0.183–0.563 seconds. [Performance and
rollout
evidence](https://loom.oa.dev/s/48pzusj4/artifacts/finelog-demand-performance-rollout).

commits.author: hrl20
commits.message:
[ops] Run the egress-report log scan in us-central2 with DuckDB httpfs (#10800)

The egress report now reads Iris task logs from the object catalog of
the finelog `log` table. Since 2026-09-03, the report read a retired
path and found no log lines.

`cross_region.py` pins the `log` catalog and selects the segments that
finelog created after `window.start - lookback`.
`ObjectQueryClient.pin_catalog()` now gives the size, the row count and
the creation time of each segment. One DuckDB query reads the selected
segments in place from GCS through httpfs. The query uses an OAuth
bearer token from the Google credentials of the job. DuckDB uses the CPU
count of the Iris task and 80% of its memory request. The DuckDB
defaults use the size of the host, and a job with an 8 GB request had an
out-of-memory failure.

`egress_report.py` runs the analysis as an Iris CPU job in us-central2,
near the log segments. Before this change, the GitHub runner downloaded
the logs from outside the region. The job writes the summary, the report
and the appendix to
`gs://marin-us-central2/tmp/ttl=1d/egress-report/<run-id>/`, because
Iris does not return the value of a callable. The runner copies these
three files. Then it creates the gist and the Discord message. The scan
stops with `QueryTimeoutError` at the catalog pin deadline, so an
expired pin cannot produce a partial report. The report files and gist
format do not change.

On 2026-10-28, a dry run with no write operations used 16 CPUs and 16
GB. It read 67 segments (16.2 GiB) for a 24-hour window in 58 s. It
found 988,575 `gs://` log lines and 9,491 cross-region mentions. That
run predates the hub-row cluster filter and the pin deadline. A run that
downloaded one segment at a time took 125 s. That run used a different
24-hour window and found 998,353 lines and the same 9,491 cross-region
mentions.

This change does not use two alternatives:

- DuckDB with gcsfs. Each read goes through Python, and the speed stayed
at approximately 210 MiB/s from 8 to 32 threads. httpfs read the same
files at 0.83 to 1.9 GiB/s with 16 to 32 threads.
- Analysis in DuckDB SQL. On 16 GiB of segments, it gave the same
summary in 25 s. The Python analysis took 63 s. The SQL version replaces
most of `analyze()`, so a different PR can add it with a test that
compares the full reports.

The catalog selection is from `rw/cross-region-catalog`. The report now
posts to #gcs-egress instead of #internal-discuss, and the `0 14 * * *`
schedule returns. The message states the share of `gs://` lines with a
known worker region and limits its "no offenders" line to that share,
because the controller loses the region of pruned workers. A window with
no `gs://` lines fails instead of posting. More data is in
https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/903.

Part of #10716

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[ci] Deal unit-test shards round-robin instead of in contiguous chunks (#10979)

Spreads the marin and levanter unit tests more evenly across their
parallel CI runners, so one overloaded runner no longer sets how long
the "Marin - Unit" check takes.

The test selector splits a large suite into shards, one per runner, by
cutting the sorted list of test files into contiguous chunks. Expensive
tests cluster by directory, so a whole cluster lands on one shard. On a
full run, marin shard 1/3 gets all 94 `experiments/` files, including
the 20-43 s `moe_hero_pipeline` and grug model tests, and shard 3/3 gets
none. In sampled CI runs from Oct 27 to Nov 5, marin 1/3 had a median of
360-380 s, while marin 2/3 and 3/3 took 190-250 s. The sharded marin leg
was the last job to finish in roughly 40% of runs.

The shards now take files round-robin from the sorted list: file 1 to
shard 1, file 2 to shard 2, and so on. Each shard keeps the same number
of files, and each directory is spread across all shards. In a full run,
the `experiments/` files split as follows.

| Leg | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| marin 1/3 | 94 | 34 |
| marin 2/3 | 8 | 34 |
| marin 3/3 | 0 | 34 |

The per-shard run times after this change have not been measured yet;
this PR's own CI gives the first data point. Round robin balances file
counts only, so two slow files can still share a shard. On levanter, for
example, `test_grugformer_moe.py` and `test_train_lm.py` now land on the
same shard. A follow-up will balance shards by measured per-file run
time once the nightly run records those times.

commits.author: muchanem
commits.message:
[rolloutengine] Allow uncapped turns and output, and expose prepare_machine (#10921)

RolloutEngine accepts three settings that Taskforge needs and that do
not change what existing callers get:

- `RolloutLimits.max_turns` accepts `None`, and the recorder then ends
an attempt only on its token budget, deadlines or a length stop.
- `ChatModel.max_tokens` accepts `None`, and the request then omits the
output limit.
- A `ChatModel.context_window`, when set, turns a `tool_calls` reply
whose prompt and completion tokens fill the window into a `length` stop.

`prepare_machine` is factored out of `task_machine`: it installs
resources and runs setup on a machine given only its requirements and
resources.

Taskforge runs its validation trials and build agents with no turn
budget and no output cap, so a session ends on its deadlines or when the
context fills, not at an arbitrary count. A full context then has to
read as a length stop, not as a pending tool call. Its build steps also
prepare machines for programs that are not yet `TaskSpec`s.

Compatibility, by change:

- `RolloutLimits.max_turns`: still required, still `gt=0`. An integer
limit validates and stops a rollout as before. Only Taskforge produces
`None` (`taskforge/spec/draft.py:237`,
`capability_driven_envs/generate_tasks_agentic.py:78`).
- Every other reader is in `vendor/skyrl`:
`skyrl_gym/nemotron_tasks.py:121`, `sql_tasks.py:256`,
`task_sessions.py:120`, `:164` and `:283`, and
`skyrl_train/rollouts/harbor_tasks.py:155`. They only ever see integers.
- The trainer lowers a canonical `TaskSpec` with its own session config
(`skyrl_train/dataset/tasks.py:186-201`), whose `max_turns` must be a
positive integer (`cloud/iris/rl_config_translation.py:243`), or takes
`int(...)` from a source row (`tasks.py:163-167`).
- The stored `TaskRolloutSpec` rows it reads back were written by that
same lowering (`tasks.py:49`, `:211`). `TaskSpec` carries no limits, so
nothing Taskforge hands on has this field.
- `ChatModel.max_tokens`, `context_window`: the only non-Taskforge
constructors are `experiments/evaluation/task_driver.py:85` and
`tests/evaluation/test_task_rollouts.py:835`, `:981`. All three pass an
integer `max_tokens` and no `context_window`, which defaults to `None`,
so their requests and stop reasons are unchanged. Nothing in
`vendor/skyrl` uses `ChatModel`.
- `prepare_machine`: new. `task_machine` delegates to it with the same
requirements, resources, runtime and cleanup deadline. Its only callers
are RolloutEngine's own tests.

The widened `max_turns` also needs two lines in
`lib/taskforge/tests/agentic/test_agent.py`: an `assert LIMITS.max_turns
is not None` before each of the two `range(LIMITS.max_turns)` calls,
which pyrefly otherwise rejects. These are the asserts Mark's 03d0e09b61
added on the Taskforge stack, moved here with the type change. Nothing
else under `agentic/` or `tests/agentic/` changes.

Nothing under `vendor/skyrl` changes here. Split out of #10298 at
forklady42's request, so the shared library's changes get one review.
#10298 depends on this PR and will carry it through `main`. Net lines:
+73 (+37 in source, +36 in tests).

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[grug] Take ring_filtered's slot-weight gradient through a gather (#10343)

Replace a slow scatter-add in the backward pass of the ring_filtered MoE
backend (#9880) with a gather. Together with #10341, this cuts June
Snowball step time by 3.0% on one 8x MI355X node and by 2.9% on two.

Before ring_filtered sends tokens to the expert shards, it fills a send
buffer with one row per (token, destination shard) pair that fits under
that shard's capacity. Each row carries the token's top-k combine
weights, with the weights for experts on other shards set to zero. It
reads each row's weights with `combine_weights_local[safe_source]`. JAX
differentiates that indexed read as a scatter-add: every row adds its
gradient back into the [tokens, top-k] weight array. A bfloat16
scatter-add on AMD GPUs uses atomic adds, which slow down sharply as
more writes hit the same memory. In MI350X profiles it took 31 ms per
step at 65536 tokens per GPU, but only 7 ms at half as many tokens.

The scatter is unnecessary because each kept (token, assignment) pair
has exactly one nonzero cell in the send buffer: its own column in the
row that goes to its expert's shard. A custom VJP uses the reverse map
from each pair to that row and gathers the pair's gradient from that
cell. Pairs without a row, which are padding tokens and pairs the sender
drops for capacity, point at a sentinel row and keep a zero gradient, as
before.

The diagram below shows this on a toy example. `g(row,k)` is the
incoming gradient for send-buffer cell (row, k).

```
Toy example: 3 tokens, top-2 routing, experts E0,E1 on shard 0 and E2,E3 on shard 1,
2 send rows per shard.   t0 -> E0,E2    t1 -> E1,E0    t2 -> E3,E1

FORWARD (unchanged): copy each token's weight row into its send rows, then zero
the columns whose expert is on the other shard.

combine_weights [T x K]   slot_weights [S x K]
         k0    k1                                 k0    k1
   t0  [ w00 | w01 ]      row 0 (t0 -> shard 0) [ w00 |  0  ]
   t1  [ w10 | w11 ]      row 1 (t1 -> shard 0) [ w10 | w11 ]
   t2  [ w20 | w21 ]      row 2 (t0 -> shard 1) [  0  | w01 ]
                          row 3 (t2 -> shard 1) [ w20 |  0  ]

   w21 is dropped: shard 0's two rows already hold t0 and t1.

BACKWARD BEFORE (autodiff scatter-add): every cotangent cell g(row,k) adds into
its row's token, zeros included. t0 has two rows, so it gets two adds per cell.

   cotangent              d combine_weights
   row 0 [ g00 |  0  ] --+
   row 2 [  0  | g21 ] --+--> t0 [ g00+0 | 0+g21 ]  <- 2 atomic adds per cell
   row 1 [ g10 | g11 ] -----> t1 [  g10  |  g11  ]
   row 3 [ g30 |  0  ] -----> t2 [  g30  |   0   ]

   8 atomic adds, 4 of them on t0, 3 of them adding zeros.

BACKWARD AFTER (custom VJP gather): each weight reads the one cell that holds
its kept copy. assignment_slot[t,k] is that row; dropped pairs get sentinel row 4.

   assignment_slot   flat = row*K + k     d combine_weights
   t0 [ 0, 2 ]       [ 0, 5 ]       ->    t0 [ g00 | g21 ]
   t1 [ 1, 1 ]       [ 2, 3 ]       ->    t1 [ g10 | g11 ]
   t2 [ 3, 4 ]       [ 6, 9 ]       ->    t2 [ g30 |  0  ]   (9 >= 8: fill 0)

   6 plain reads, no atomics, same result.
```

Step times on June Snowball on MI355X (EP8, batch 128 per node,
save_moe, PGLE). These numbers combine this change with the AMD
cross-entropy backward block (#10341):

| Setup | Before (s/step) | After (s/step) | Step time change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| One 8x MI355X node | 2.523 | 2.448 | -3.0% |
| Two 8x MI355X nodes (EP8 x DP2, batch 256) | 3.198 | 3.106 | -2.9% |

The same pair of changes also helps on one 8x MI350X node (2.906 to
2.805 s/step, -3.5%). Measured alone on a one-GPU MI350X stand-in for
one EP8 rank, this change reduces step time by 1.3%. Losses are
unchanged, and the ring_filtered tests pass on MI350X.

This applies directly to main now that #9880 has merged. It edits code
next to #10345's change in `ep_ring_filtered.py`, so whichever of the
two merges second needs a rebase that keeps both custom VJPs. Part of
#9812.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[rl] Recover installed agents from context overflow (#10844)

An installed agent can recover when a request exceeds the model's
context limit. SkyRL returns a context-length error so the agent can
shorten its conversation and try again. RolloutEngine omits the rejected
request from the record and keeps the turn and time limits in force.
Native harnesses still stop at the length limit.

The installed-agent endpoint completes a streamed model request before
sending response headers. A context rejection therefore reaches OpenCode
as HTTP 400 JSON; successful responses still use SSE. In an OpenCode
1.18.2 probe, the previous SSE error became `UnknownError` and ended the
run. HTTP 400 became `ContextOverflowError`, followed by compaction and
another model request.

When SkyRL resumes from sampled tokens, vLLM checks the prompt tokens it
will actually serve. Reconstructing the chat can use more tokens than
the sampled prompt. That longer reconstruction no longer blocks a prompt
that fits. vLLM still rejects an oversized prompt.

Co-authored-by: Ben Feuer <benfeuer@Bens-MacBook-Pro.local>

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[zephyr] Authenticate Polars Parquet scans with file-delivered keys (#10899)

Zephyr Parquet reads through Polars now work inside Iris task pods,
where #10474 delivers storage keys as mounted files instead of
environment variables.

Polars' Rust object_store client reads credentials from the environment
alone. Task pods carry the submitted CoreWeave pair only as named files
and an `AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE` profile, which that client ignores,
so its chain fell through to instance metadata and CoreWeave answered
404. FULL curation campaigns on cw-us-east-02a failed at the scatter
merge (`pl.merge_sorted`) with that error while every fsspec-based read
and write succeeded.

Rigging resolves the bucket's declared store file-first and hands the
static key pair to Polars as storage options; undeclared buckets, non-S3
paths, and credential-less stores keep the ambient chain. The existing
virtual-host endpoint qualification still applies and merges with the
credentials.

Co-authored-by: Ben Feuer <benfeuer@Bens-MacBook-Pro.local>

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[marina] Copy rolloutengine into the Marina image (#10966)

Copy `lib/rolloutengine` into the Marina image. `marin-core` has
depended on `marin-rolloutengine`
since #10757, but the Dockerfile and its build-context allowlist never

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[harbor] Route task and verifier execution through Shellbox (#10628)

Run Harbor task commands and grading scripts through Shellbox. Replace
Harbor's independent environment-provider backends and custom
environment imports with adapters for local bubblewrap (the default),
Daytona, QEMU and ShellSim. Marin invokes Harbor as an isolated binary;
Shellbox has no Harbor dependency.

Translate a validated Compose subset into Shellbox tasks with prepared,
digest-pinned images. Local tasks keep agent and runtime containers
alive on private loopback with external traffic denied. Tau3 retains its
runtime, candidate agent and grading script. Reject unsupported Compose
fields, host mounts, runtime sockets and privileged operations before
execution. Resolve task environment and working-directory settings once
and retain the imported plan through startup.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant D as Trusted Marin/Harbor driver
    participant A as Agent container
    participant R as Tau3 runtime container
    participant P as Model provider
    participant F as FineStore
    D->>A: Create Shellbox task and loopback HTTP helpers
    A->>D: Candidate request on port 8788 via process pipes
    D->>P: Forward to configured candidate model with host credentials
    P-->>D: Complete response
    D-->>A: Bounded response over process pipes
    A->>R: Task-local MCP runtime request
    R->>A: User-model request on loopback port 8787
    A->>D: Request over persistent process pipes
    D->>P: Forward to configured judge model with host credentials
    P-->>D: Complete response
    D-->>A: Bounded response over process pipes
    A-->>R: HTTP response
    D->>R: Collect runtime logs after agent finishes
    D->>A: Run grading script, then close task containers
    D->>F: Commit native result and trajectory presence atomically
```

Capture host credentials once at each executable entry point and pass
them outside serialized configuration. Normalize model endpoints,
explicit credential sources and guest aliases in Harbor's
host-capability module. Candidate authentication uses a private driver
channel, preserving policy judge credentials. A hosted judge replaces
policy judge authority and maps both OpenAI URL aliases and all model
roles to its relay. Guest templates resolve only declared inputs; cloud,
storage, controller credentials and known host secrets are rejected at
guest boundaries. Host-side agents use captured authentication.
Installed local and Daytona agents call fixed loopback relays, which
expose bounded chat, text Responses and tokenization routes. Streaming
chat is buffered. Verifier-only judge access opens during grading; Tau3
and Sotopia allow judge-model requests during agent execution. Marin
preflight rejects Codex and Claude Code because their required protocols
exceed that relay contract. Saved configuration redacts Iris bearer
URLs. Harbor retains storage authority for uploads; #10819 tracks
removing it.

Discover local cgroup delegation within the worker's own cgroup or its
empty systemd unit above `DelegateSubgroup`. Command cancellation reaps
descendants while preserving files, earlier successful services and
runtime peers. CPU and memory declarations are numeric limits applied
independently where controllers permit, with warnings when enforcement
is unavailable. Local Harbor rejects `ignore` resource policies and
still requires working recursive process containment. Before
verifier-only judge access, it stops remaining agent command groups.
Grading without verifier-only judge access preserves successful
services. Terminus interrupts its foreground terminal job on
cancellation, treats zombie-only groups as stopped, and releases tmux at
teardown.

A trial owns required relay tasks through setup, execution, collection,
grading and teardown. Relay, log collection and teardown failures are
named, retryable infrastructure errors and remain unscored. Publish
final native results after teardown and required artifact writes. Commit
native attempt results, available ATIF trajectories and presence
metadata atomically; normalize selected results into FineStore samples,
steps and rollouts. Incomplete attempts retain evidence and can recover
through resume or a successful retry. An incomplete selected attempt or
missing declared trajectory prevents sealing. Candidate and judge
serving routes may change while their recorded model identities remain
unchanged. Evaluator identity uses Rigging launch provenance and Marin
artifacts. Any change to the tracked Marin tree invalidates cache and
resume reuse; missing provenance fails before reuse. No separate
source-file hashing is added.

Pi and Pi/ACP use image-provided binaries; setup stages configuration
without package downloads. Standalone Pi requires a declared,
digest-pinned prepared main image before model allocation; Daytona's
task image must match. BixBench and BFCL standalone Pi campaign policies
now fail preflight until their tasks are prepared, and verified-cohort
use requires updating their approved source digests. Marin no longer
installs Pi 0.87.0 during setup: the image supplies its version, checked
when explicitly requested. The Tau3 image supplies Pi 0.80.5 for
standalone and ACP use. Pi's MCP configuration is a packaged JavaScript
asset. Tau3's bridge excludes conversation-control tools from the
candidate while retaining domain tools, and checks canonical runtime
status before advancing the conversation. Runtime MCP failures retain
infrastructure classification; candidate process failures retain agent
classification. The `tau3_image()` helper reuses or builds images keyed
by their Dockerfile, dependency locks and build settings in
`ghcr.io/marin-community/rollout-images`. Task preparation pins runtime
images containing each task's server and configuration. Sandbox
executables belong on the trusted evaluator host; the Iris task
Dockerfile supplies them separately from rollout guest dependencies.

Use the Shellbox execution contract from #10640. Native Iris task groups
remain in separate draft #10822; no controller rollout is required.
Daytona policies require an explicit `DAYTONA_TARGET` before model
allocation. Launches using `eval-policy-2026-09-24-verified` use carried
evaluator identity instead of requiring the historical Harbor source
pin. Compose groups currently use local bubblewrap; Daytona supports
single-machine execution and hosted grading. Confirmed cleanup of
detached command descendants is a local guarantee. Daytona cannot
exclude an independently surviving candidate process during grading.
Runtime model access is reachable by peers sharing the task network.
Private verifier access combined with a live agent-started service
requires separate isolation. Bubblewrap shares the host kernel and
requires namespace permissions and delegated containment; installing its
executables alone is insufficient. Prepared local images require root
`USER`. A companion exiting closes the entire local task, including its
agent, so grading cannot continue in that task. Disk quotas and
accelerator allocation remain unsupported. Existing resume roots without
evaluator identity require a new root.

Tau3 ACP trials retain raw ACPX exports and produce scored FineStore
samples. They do not declare an ATIF trajectory: ACPX exports are not
converted to ATIF, so these trials have no derived step or rollout rows.
Presence metadata records the expected absence.

commits.message:
loom: add a belay profile and a disabled belay watch for Marin Belay sessions (#10824)

Adds a `belay` Loom profile and a disabled `belay` watch, so Marin Belay
sessions can run on Loom instead of a maintainer's laptop. A session
reads `experiments/belay/RUNBOOK.md` on `marin_belay_v1_recipe` and runs
only `uv run python -m experiments.belay <command>`.

Profile:

- One session at a time (`maxConcurrent: 1`), `envClear`, strict
automation, `marin-community/marin` only.
- Env: `IRIS_USER=loom` and the shared Claude token, like the other
Claude automation profiles, plus three secrets:
- `WANDB_API_KEY` from `BELAY_WANDB_API_KEY`, a `marin-community` W&B
service-account key. The fast_track launcher refuses to submit without
it and passes it to each job.
- `CW_KEY_ID` and `CW_KEY_SECRET` from `BELAY_CW_KEY_ID` and
`BELAY_CW_KEY_SECRET`, a CoreWeave access key for Belay. Since #10475
every CoreWeave job carries its submitter's keys, so this key's access
policy is what bounds Belay runs: read the training and eval data, read
and write `tmp/ttl=*/belay/*`, read profiles under `tmp/ttl=*/xprof/*`,
nothing else.
- Replies on the intake issue (#9514) use Loom's GitHub App token; no
bot token is needed.

Trigger: an agent watch, `every: 10m`, `runTimeoutSeconds: 14400`,
`enabled: false`, with the prompt in `watches/belay.md`. Each run starts
with `start --check-only`, which reads the Belay app's public state and
ends the session at once unless events are queued and no session is
active. If there is work, the session claims the events (`claim`),
follows the runbook and its drain loop (`wait`) until nothing short is
left, and reports back with `finish`. A zero-token script watch could
also start the session (script watches with the `launch` capability call
`/runs/create`). But a script watch's program has to be a file already
on the Loom server, while this agent watch is declared entirely in this
stack.

Before enabling the watch:

- A CoreWeave org admin creates the Belay access key and policy, and its
two halves are uploaded as `BELAY_CW_KEY_ID` and `BELAY_CW_KEY_SECRET`.
Preview fails until both secrets exist.
- The Belay Marina app (#10829) has to be released. Its agent endpoints
accept `loom-vm@hai-gcp-models.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.
- The Belay client (`experiments/belay/page.py`) still sends only a
service token, so it needs to present the session's identity to Marina
through IAP.

`claim`, `finish` and `start --check-only` are on the Belay tooling
branches; they are not part of this PR.

Part of #9451

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Add optional log scaling of hero global queries (#10923)

Add an optional `log_scaling_n_floor` to the hero model for the 262K
query temperature comparison. Only `launch_diagnostics.py
--log-scaling-n-floor` sets it. The hero configuration leaves it off.

- On global layers, the model multiplies a query that sees `n` keys in
its document by `1 + 0.1 * ln(max(n / floor, 1))`. This factor applies
on top of `qk_mult` and `qk_mult_long_scale`.
- The form comes from
[Inkling](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/inkling/modeling_inkling.py).
Inkling uses absolute position as `n`. This change counts keys in the
document, because a packed row holds several documents. Inkling also
scales a relative-position bias, which the hero model does not have.
- At the end of a 262K document with `qk_mult` 1.66, a floor of 65536
gives an effective 1.890. A floor of 128000 gives 1.779.
- The change adds no parameters and does not change kernels,
checkpoints, or optimizer state.
- With the field unset, jaxprs and logits match the base commit at CP1
and CP4 on CPU. The advisory artifact fingerprint changes, but the
artifact path does not.
- In a one-off run on one GB200 node, real FA4 zigzag ran forward and
backward at bf16. The run used a 4096-token model and a floor of 256.
The mean CP4 versus CP1 logit gap was 0.00045 with scaling on and
0.00042 with scaling off. The on-versus-off effect was 0.0055.
- We did not measure the real 262K shape, training quality, or step
time. No evidence yet shows an improvement.
- The vLLM fork and SkyRL apply a fixed scale per layer, so they would
use the wrong temperature past the floor. `to_hf_config` now raises an
error for this field, which stops the Hero exports and the upload.
Long-context evals through vLLM cannot measure these arms, so they use
native evaluation.
- `launch_diagnostics.py` refuses a floor at or above the sequence
length, because that run would scale no query.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[finelog] Bound query reads and remove cache visibility contention (#10929)

Apply the default ten-second read budget before admission so queueing,
visibility waits, provider construction, execution, and encoding share
one
deadline. Bound optional cache downloads by that deadline and enforce
the
256 MiB allowance without admitting an oversized final object.

Pin cached files per read so eviction skips active inputs without
queuing a
global visibility writer. Object compaction updates its accounting view
without
waiting for readers. Preserve visibility protection for legacy file
replacement
and table deletion.

Route object-backed Parquet, index, projection, and maintenance reads
through
the cache-aware object-store range interface, preserving coalesced
requests,
footer caching, and scan-byte counters. Read index headers and required
sections
from cache or GCS/S3 without downloading whole bundles. Concurrent
segment
pruning shares a 500 ms index-I/O budget and checks key sections first;
unavailable indexes retain the source scan. Preserve same-column
substring
alternatives during trigram pruning and support string equality
predicates.

The November 4 hub incident recorded 256 GB of query cache fills over 51
minutes
while unrelated reads waited on visibility:
https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/926.

---------

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[snowball-tpu] [eval] Check Snowball TPU and H100 logprob parity (#10607)

Check Snowball's frozen next-token probabilities through H100 and
multi-host TPU vLLM instead of comparing benchmark accuracy. Both arms
use the same 64 exact token-ID prompts across 256–32768-token buckets,
require coverage of the frozen top-25 tokens, apply the existing
explained-winner rule and 0.125 probability bound, and require exact
same-process recomputation of the long-prompt sentinel.

Extract the endpoint-scoring loop from the existing H100 check and reuse
it for v4-32 at TP16. Keep the coordinator on CPU while isolated TPU
children enable both TPU and CPU JAX backends. Launch the Ray supervisor
with Python safe-path mode so its sibling `types.py` cannot shadow the
standard library. Remove the accuracy evaluator and comparator.

Each job has a one-hour runtime, bounded queue, zero retries and fresh
result paths. The TPU arm reads the verified regional mirror of the
exact June d819 export.

Verification: 24 focused HTTP-contract, probability, entrypoint and Ray
regression tests pass; required lint/type checks and advisory review are
clean. Task #336 measured two fresh processes per arm: maximum
probability errors were 0.074066 on H100, 0.093186 on v5p-8 and 0.073077
on v4-32, all below 0.125. Live H100 and v4-32 checks also pass all 64
prompts and exact same-process repeatability, with maximum probability
errors of 0.074066 and 0.059369 respectively.
